theory.intro: In similar figures every pair of corresponding sides is in the same ratio, so one known pair unlocks all the rest. Find the scale factor from the pair with **both lengths given**, then multiply or divide by it.
facts: $k=\frac{\text{image length}}{\text{original length}}$, found from the pair of corresponding sides with both lengths given.
Multiply an original side by $k$ to get the matching **image** side; divide an image side by $k$ to get the **original**.
If the image is smaller than the original then $k<1$, so multiplying by it correctly shortens the sides.
The same working can be set out as equal fractions of corresponding sides, e.g. $\frac{x}{6}=\frac{14}{4}$ — keep the unknown in the numerator.
steps: Identify the pair of corresponding sides with both lengths given.
Calculate the scale factor: divide the image length by the original length.
Multiply an original side by the scale factor, or divide an image side by it, to find the unknown side.

workedExamples.solution_text:
Match the bases, vertical sides and sloping sides.

| Original | Image |
| --- | --- |
| $6$ | $9$ |
| $4$ | $x$ |
| $y$ | $7.5$ |

$k=\frac{\text{image length}}{\text{original length}}=\frac{9}{6}=1.5$

Multiply to find the image side.
$\begin{align*}x&=4\times1.5\\x&=6\text{ cm}\end{align*}$

Divide to find the original side.
$\begin{align*}y&=7.5\div1.5\\y&=5\text{ cm}\end{align*}$

The $16$ cm and $8$ cm sides correspond.
$k=\frac{8}{16}=0.5$

Multiply the original side by the scale factor, even when the factor is less than $1$.
$\begin{align*}x&=12\times0.5\\x&=6\text{ cm}\end{align*}$

$DE$ corresponds to $AB$, and $EF$ corresponds to $BC$.
$k=\frac{DE}{AB}=\frac{10}{5}=2$

$\begin{align*}x&=13\times2\\x&=26\text{ cm}\end{align*}$

Sam matched a short side with a long side. The $6$ cm side corresponds to the $4$ cm side; $x$ corresponds to the $10$ cm side.

$k=\frac{6}{4}=1.5$

$\begin{align*}x&=10\times1.5\\x&=15\text{ cm}\end{align*}$

mastery.question_text:
Two similar triangles have corresponding sides of $7.2$ cm (original) and $18$ cm (image).
Another side of the original is $11.6$ cm long.
Find the length of the corresponding side of the image.

mastery.solution_text:
Ben matched the image's $10$ cm side with the original's $15$ cm side, but the $10$ cm side is the image's short side, so it corresponds to the original's $6$ cm side.
$k=\frac{10}{6}=\frac{5}{3}$
$x=15\times\frac{5}{3}$
$=25\text{ cm}$
